thread:
maya: heads up :wave: saw ~12 preemptible evictions in us-west2 over the last 15m that impacted in-flight streaming requests (some partial token drops). digging into patterns now
liam: ugh. what's our current graceful termination window for the runtime pods?
maya: default SIGTERM wait is 10s. kube node preempt notice arrives ~30s before reclaim, but our pod gets kill earlier due to eviction controller. logs show runtime starts shutdown and drops open stream after ~8s
raj: 10s won't cut it for streaming. either we extend pod drain or implement resume-token cutover so clients can reconnect and continue a stream
olivia: +1 on resume-token. idea: on SIGTERM emit a "final-chunk" packet with a resume token header and snapshot minimal KV state to redis S3 within N ms, then requeue the remaining request on fallback pool
sophia: what fallback pool? reserved capacity? cold start cost tradeoff is real if we move many streams to reserved GPUs
maya: thinking mixed strategy: short streams (<2s remaining) just flush and finish within extended drain (40s). long streams -> emit resume-token and requeue to reserved or to another spot instance if available. prefer reserved for high-SLA tenants
deploy-bot: eviction_notice: instance-spot-43 preempt at 2026-06-12T03:21:10Z TTL=30s
liam: config sketch (proposal):
```
eviction_policy:
  preemptible_grace_seconds: 45
  stream_resume_token: true
  kv_snapshot_target: redis://evict-snapshots
  fallback_pools:
    - reserved-gpu-pool
    - spot-warm-pool
  requeue_latency_target_ms: 300
```
oliivia: (typo) -> olivia: we should be explicit about token size and storage TTL. resume-token must be opaque id, TTL 2m by default, retriable up to 3 attempts
raj: implementation notes: runtime should do minimal sync: write {token_id -> last_sequence_idx, model_version, kv_digest} to redis in <50ms. clients will call /stream/resume?token=<id> and server will rehydrate short-term cache then continue. for long-term resume we fallback to full request re-run which is expensive
sophia: ops concern: increasing preemptible_grace_seconds increases spot hold time and could raise $/token. need cost delta estimate before we flip for all tenants
maya: rollout plan: canary 5% (dev org), monitor metrics: eviction_count, stream_resume_rate, resume_success_rate, requeue_latency, cost_delta_pct. if resume_success_rate >= 95% and requeue_latency < 500ms we widen to 25% then 100%
ops-bot: added monitor:stream_resume_rate to dashboard "Stream Resilience" and alert on <90% for 15m
liam: one more nuance: partial tokens already sent to clients — for HTTP streaming we send last packet with `X-Resume-Token`. for websocket we send a control frame. need client SDK changes (python/js) + server header contract
olivia: SDK TODOs: auto-reconnect with exponential backoff, resume header injection, metric for resumed_sessions. I'll draft PR
raj: test plan: simulate forced evictions in staging with short/long streams, assert no more than 1% token loss and that resume path restores correctness for 99% of flows. also load test redis snapshot path under 1k writes/s
maya: blockers: infra change to allow longer graceful drain in node-pool autoscaler (cloud quota may reject). @raj can you check GCE quotas and whether autoscaler honors preempt TTL extension?
raj: on it. I'll also estimate cost for 45s vs 10s grace on a sample of 10k evictions/day
liam: timeline?
maya: aim for canary by EOW if no quota blockers. olivia/raj to open PRs and run staging sims. will post follow-ups here. :thumbsup:
